summary: AccessGuard (password-protected shares) fully verified. 25/25 backend pytest pass (13 legacy DropBoxer + 12 new AccessGuard). Full frontend E2E flow verified via Playwright: protect-with-password checkbox reveals password input, upload button correctly disabled while protect on and password empty, protected share shows Protection row 'Password required' in ResultCard, /share/:id renders password-entry input + unlock button (no download-securely-button), wrong password shows password-error-message, unprotected share regression still shows download-securely-button, My Shares dashboard card shows Lock icon for protected shares. Backend Mongo doc contains bcrypt hash starting with $2b$ (verified directly), passwordHash never leaks in /api/share, /api/shares or upload response.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py verify_share_password uses body.get('password').strip() — trims whitespace before verify. If a user intentionally sets a password with leading/trailing spaces at upload (which is hashed as-is), verify would fail. Consider trimming symmetrically at hash time or not trimming here. Low priority since UI trims too.

GET /api/download/:id with ?pw= passes the password through the URL/query string; while the endpoint itself supports it for API clients, this is only safe because the SharePage.jsx uses POST /api/verify instead. Consider adding a docstring warning or dropping ?pw= support to avoid future misuse (passwords in access logs).
Still no rate-limit / lockout on POST /api/verify — infinite brute-force attempts possible. Add throttle (e.g. 5 attempts / minute per shareId+IP) before production.
Carryover from iteration_1: non-atomic burn (find_one_and_update then separate status:'USED' update) and sync aws_service calls from async endpoints — not blocking for AccessGuard.
